app.name: Hematologist+
app.disclaimer: Decision-support tool. Final dosing and prescribing decisions rest with the physician.

patient.title: Patient
patient.note: Patient data is never sent anywhere and never stored: it lives only in this browser tab.
patient.sexMissing: Choose the sex: the creatinine clearance is not calculated without it
patient.bsaNone: BSA not calculated (no height and weight)
patient.orEnterBsa: or enter the BSA by hand

clearanceWeight.label: Weight for the clearance:
clearanceWeight.hint: BMI {{bmi}} kg/m². Which weight to use in Cockcroft-Gault with obesity is unresolved (UpToDate): most use the actual one, the GOG the adjusted one (IBW + 0.4 × (actual − IBW)) from a BMI of 25. The chosen weight goes into the clearance, the renal corrections and carboplatin.

course.title: Course
course.noRegimens: There are no regimens in the catalog yet.
course.cycleNumberHint: the first antibody infusion is the slow one
course.dayStartHint: 11:00 by default; change it by hand
course.bsaM2Hint: used instead of the one calculated from height and weight
course.phasesHint: The phase follows the cycle number; maintenance or consolidation is chosen here.

hospital.title: Sheet header
hospital.head: Head of department
hospital.none: No institutions in the catalog; fill the fields in manually.

doses.title: Doses
doses.premedAlert: The department gives {{drugs}} only with premedication, and the label asks for it before every dose. Switch the premedication rows on, or leave them off on purpose.
doses.concentrationRange: Allowed concentration by the label: {{min}}–{{max}} mg/mL
doses.concentrationMax: Allowed concentration by the label: up to {{max}} mg/mL
doses.concentrationMin: Allowed concentration by the label: at least {{min}} mg/mL
doses.concentrationNone: The label sets no concentration limits; the volume is as it states
doses.continuousDoxorubicinBag: The department standard is 500 mL a day; the label sets no concentration limits
doses.durationStretched: The dose is large for this duration: the infusion is worked out over {{duration}}
doses.bolusHint: The protocol's daily dose is split equally; the first bolus goes with the start of the ifosfamide (cyclophosphamide), or of the day's first cytostatic without it. Each dose is rounded up to whole ampoules.

block.day_support: Support on the infusion day (infusion sheet)

doses.addInvalidDays: List the course days as comma-separated numbers
doses.modifiersHint: Several may be ticked; the lowest dose applies
doses.irradiatedHint: After the BSH 2020 guideline. The sheet will say so; tell the transfusion laboratory and mark the request.
doses.rampLine: {{days}} — {{kind}}: {{start}} mL/h, +{{step}} every {{every}} min, up to {{max}} mL/h (≈{{minutes}} min)

renal.off: Correction off: for CrCl {{crcl}} mL/min (range {{min}}-{{max}}) the label gives {{corrected}}; the calculation uses {{protocol}}
renal.above: CrCl {{crcl}} mL/min, above {{above}}: no renal correction needed
renal.unchecked: Renal correction not checked: no creatinine clearance (needs creatinine, age, sex and weight). The dose is as in the regimen.
renal.notForDose: The correction by clearance is written for the regimen dose only; it is not calculated for the dose chosen. Check the drug caution.
renal.keepProtocol: Do not correct (dose and interval as in the regimen)
renal.withheld: CrCl {{crcl}} mL/min (range {{min}}-{{max}}): {{corrected}} The drug is not calculated.
renal.withheldOff: Correction off: for CrCl {{crcl}} mL/min (range {{min}}-{{max}}) {{corrected}} The calculation uses {{protocol}}.

withhold.not_recommended: the label does not recommend the drug.
withhold.levels: the doses after the first follow the drug level in the blood.

renal.range: The label gives a range, not one dose: {{min}}-{{max}} {{unit}} per administration ({{dayMin}}-{{dayMax}} {{unit}} a day). Choose where in it to dose:
renal.firstDose: The first dose in full, as in the regimen, uncorrected for the kidneys (as the source says); the ones after it are corrected, in the row below.

everyOtherDay.label: How to give the corrected dose
everyOtherDay.note: Alternative: the full dose every other day gives the same total from whole capsules (no oral liquid of fluconazole is registered in Ukraine). Neither the SmPC nor UpToDate describes it directly; the physician decides.

doses.ivigSupportOn: 3 lines added above the immunoglobulin: hydration with KCl and MgSO4, paracetamol, dexamethasone with diphenhydramine. Edit them as text.
doses.ivigSupportOff: Hydration, paracetamol and dexamethasone with diphenhydramine, as on the department sheet.

standardSupport.title: Standard support
standardSupport.lead: Antiemetics and infection prophylaxis are switched on and off here with one switch. If the regimen has its own rows of the kind, the switch enables or disables them; if it has none, it adds the standard ones.

standard.antiemetic: Adds ondansetron 8 mg twice a day on the days cytostatics are given
standard.antiviral: Adds aciclovir 400 mg twice a day for the whole cycle
standard.pneumocystis: Adds co-trimoxazole 480 mg on Mon, Wed and Fri
standard.antifungal: Adds fluconazole 50 mg a day for the whole cycle
standard.antibacterial: Adds levofloxacin 500 mg once a day for the whole cycle

thromboAgent.apixaban: Apixaban 2.5 mg twice a day for the whole cycle (NSSG standard)
thromboAgent.enoxaparin: Enoxaparin 40 mg SC once a day for the whole cycle
thromboAgent.aspirin: Aspirin 100 mg once a day for the whole cycle, only with no other risk factor

antiviralAgent.aciclovir: Adds aciclovir 400 mg twice a day for the whole cycle
antiviralAgent.valaciclovir: Adds valaciclovir 500 mg twice a day for the whole cycle

manual.title: Lines written by hand
manual.lead: An order the catalog does not hold: printed as it is typed, never calculated. A whole sheet can be made this way, with no regimen at all.

support.title: Optional support
support.hint: Bags of 500, 1000 and 3000 mL come with potassium and magnesium in proportion (per 1000 mL: KCl 4% 40 mL, MgSO4 25% 4 mL); either can be switched off or changed. Nothing is filled in for smaller bags (100–400 mL): switch it on and type the amount. The line can be edited below.

schedule.title: Schedule
schedule.wardNote: A shift moves the infusions and the support hung off them. Rows of the inpatient sheet have no clock time and never move.

export.title: Export to Excel
export.hint: The department blanks: a sheet for every day with an administration plus the inpatient prescription list (form 003-4/o). The file is built in the browser: patient data is never sent anywhere.
export.hintWard: One prescription list (form No. 003-4/o) for the whole course: every drug a line, «+» on the days it is given and «-» on the days it is not. The file is built in the browser: no patient data is sent anywhere.
export.irradiated: Say on the sheet: irradiated blood components only
export.irradiatedHint: The regimen shows no reason. Tick it for one in the history: Hodgkin lymphoma, purine analogues, HSCT, CAR-T.

error.title: Calculation failed
error.dosingWeight: An aminoglycoside (amikacin) is dosed on the ideal or adjusted weight, which needs the height and sex. Enter the sex and height; the calculator does not fall back to the actual weight, which would overdose an obese patient.

tabs.empty: The result appears here once there is a patient and a regimen (or hand-written lines).

requirements.title: To calculate the course and print the sheets, enter:
requirements.invalid: The patient data hold an error: correct the marked field.

reason.bsa: {{fields}}: for a dose per m² (or enter the BSA by hand): {{drugs}}
reason.dosingWeight: {{fields}}: for a dose on the ideal or adjusted weight: {{drugs}}
reason.clearance: {{fields}}: for the dose correction by creatinine clearance: {{drugs}}

requirements.supportUnadjusted: Without {{fields}} the prophylaxis is printed at the usual dose, not checked against the creatinine clearance: {{drugs}}

need.title: Drug need
need.lead: The Ministry's distribution form, «Узагальнена інформація щодо розподілу лікарських засобів, медичних виробів до проєкту наказу». It needs nothing about any patient — it counts how many there are.

form.title: Graphs of the form
form.name: Name as the order writes it
form.nameHint: trade name and strength, as in the order
form.monthlyUseHint: counted as patients × packs per course
form.monthsHint: counted as 100 % need ÷ average monthly use
form.proposedHint: the whole need unless typed over

hint.title: Hint for the count
hint.lead: How many packs one course takes. The regimens need not have anything to do with each other: the form is filled in drug by drug. A pack other than the line's own is shown only for orientation.
hint.bsaHint: a typical body surface of the department's patients
hint.empty: Choose a drug in a line of the form and a regimen to count by appears here.
hint.noRegimen: No regimen of the catalog gives this drug — enter the need by hand.

export.title: File to hand in
export.hint: The distribution form as .xlsx, printed A4 landscape. The hint for the count is not written to the file.

diseases.title: Diseases
diseases.empty: The list of diseases is empty so far.

diseaseDetail.situationNone: No regimen fits every chosen situation
diseaseDetail.title: Disease

step.dose.weight.ideal: Dosing weight is the ideal {{idealKg}} kg ({{heightCm}} cm): the actual {{actualKg}} kg is within 120% of it
step.dose.weight.adjusted: Dosing weight is adjusted: {{idealKg}} + 0.4 × ({{actualKg}} − {{idealKg}}) kg, since the actual is above 120% of the ideal ({{heightCm}} cm)
step.dose.cap: Limited by the maximum dose of {{capAmount}} {{unit}}
step.renal.cockcroftGault: Cockcroft-Gault creatinine clearance (creatinine {{serumCreatinineMgDl}} mg/dL, sex factor {{sexFactor}})
step.infusion.volume: Volume: {{bagVolumeMl}} mL of solvent + {{drugVolumeMl}} mL of drug
step.infusion.ramp: Rate raised in steps: {{startMlH}} mL/h, +{{stepMlH}} every {{everyMin}} min, up to {{maxMlH}} mL/h (later infusions {{nextDurationMin}} min)
step.infusion.maxRate: No faster than {{maxRateMgMin}} mg/min: infusion {{durationMin}} min instead of {{regimenMin}}
step.infusion.rate: Rate over {{durationMin}} min ({{rateGttMin}} drops/min, giving set {{dropFactor}} drops/mL)

step.renal.bandAbove: CrCl above {{aboveMlMin}} mL/min: dose and interval not corrected
step.renal.bandRange: Dose within the label range of {{rangeMin}}-{{rangeMax}} {{unit}} per administration

warning.input.outOfRange: {{field}}: {{value}} is outside {{min}}–{{max}}. Check the entered data.
warning.bsa.capped: Actual BSA {{actualM2}} m² exceeds {{capM2}} m². Both dose variants are shown.
warning.bsa.enteredDiffers: The entered BSA {{enteredM2}} m² differs from the one calculated from height and weight ({{calculatedM2}} m²) by {{differencePercent}}%. Check the value.
warning.dose.capped: Dose limited by the maximum ({{capAmount}} {{unit}}); the regimen would give {{baseAmount}} {{unit}}.
warning.carboplatin.gfrCapped: GFR capped at {{capMlMin}} mL/min for the Calvert formula.
warning.infusion.concentrationOutOfRange: Concentration {{concentration}} {{unit}} is outside the allowed range. Check the solvent volume.
warning.review.lowCreatinineClearance: Creatinine clearance {{value}} mL/min is below {{threshold}}. Consider a reduction.
warning.review.highBilirubin: Bilirubin {{value}} µmol/L is above {{threshold}}. Consider a reduction.
warning.title: Note
warning.noDoseChange: Warnings never change a dose — the decision rests with the physician.
warning.review.clearanceUnknown: Creatinine clearance not calculated: {{field}} is missing. Check renal function separately.
warning.review.ageUnknown: Age is not given, so the age-based review hints are not shown.
warning.renal.bandUnchecked: No creatinine clearance: the renal correction (below {{belowMlMin}} mL/min) is not checked. The dose and interval are as in the regimen.
warning.renal.bandNotForDose: The correction by clearance is written for the regimen dose only; it is not calculated for the dose chosen.
warning.renal.bandOff: Renal correction switched off: for CrCl {{clearanceMlMin}} mL/min the label gives {{doseValue}} {{unit}} every {{everyH}} h.
warning.renal.withheldOff.not_recommended: Renal correction switched off: at CrCl {{clearanceMlMin}} mL/min the label does not recommend the drug.
warning.renal.withheldOff.levels: Renal correction switched off: at CrCl {{clearanceMlMin}} mL/min the doses after the first follow the drug level in the blood.

sources.title: Sources
sources.intro: The official designs and protocols the calculation rests on. Every dose, dilution and rate names its document and the date it was checked.
sources.empty: No sources in the catalog yet.
sources.staleTitle: The data may be out of date
sources.stale: Every document shows its own date (version) and the date its values were taken. Drug lists and registration details go stale: check the pack against the State Register of Medicinal Products of Ukraine (drlz.com.ua) before ordering, and the dose against the current protocol.

error.title: Something went wrong
error.body: The page could not be shown. Usually the saved offline copy of the catalog, written by an earlier version, is the cause. Clear it and reload: no patient data is stored anywhere, so nothing is lost.
error.reset: Clear the saved copy and reload

proposals.title: Proposals
proposals.intro: What to add or fix in the catalog. A proposal is seen by you and by the owner of the project; the answer appears on the same card.
proposals.signInReason: Sign in with the department account to send a proposal.
proposals.noPatientData: Nothing about a patient here: no name, no case number, no date of birth. The text is stored on the server.
proposals.subject: In short
proposals.bodyHint: What exactly is needed: a regimen (with its protocol if you have it), a drug, an article, a mistake in the calculation.

auth.title: Department sign-in
auth.hint: Articles are available to signed-in users only. Accounts are created by the administrator; there is no self-registration.
auth.articleLocked: The article text is available after signing in.
auth.articleEmpty: Nothing written for this source yet.

regimen.title: Regimen
regimen.trialNote: The doses come from a published study, not from a guideline or a label. Check the indication and agree the use before prescribing.

levelScale.oxford-cebm-2011: Oxford Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine, 2011 levels of evidence

levelValue.1: 1 — a systematic review of randomised trials
levelValue.4: 4 — a case series or a single-arm study

verdict.caution: Caution: the regimen works, but the study found a harm that calls for patient selection or prophylaxis. See the conduct notes.
verdict.avoid: Do not use: a randomised study found no benefit or found harm. Kept only as a warning.

scores.title: Scores and formulas
scores.lead: Everyday formulas for the haematology patient and risk and prognostic scores. The cut-offs and points of each were checked against the publication named under it (2026-10-11). The result helps, it does not replace clinical judgement.
scores.fill: Fill in the fields to see the result.
scores.invalid: A value is out of range — check what was entered.

irradiated.title: Conditions that need irradiated blood components
irradiated.lead: Irradiating cellular components prevents transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease, rare and nearly always fatal. The list follows the British Society for Haematology guideline (BSH 2020).
irradiated.gradeHint: Grade as GRADE in the guideline: 1 strong, 2 weak recommendation; A–C quality of evidence.

immunodeficiency.title: Treatment-related risk factors
immunodeficiency.lead: Which drugs and regimens of haematological cancer treatment cause secondary immunodeficiency, which infections it brings and what the guidelines advise. The chips above pick the drugs by risk.
immunodeficiency.general: Factors that add risk with any treatment
immunodeficiency.sources: Sources (in brackets: source number and grade)
immunodeficiency.alertTitle: Treatment-related infection risk: what the guidelines advise

febrileNeutropenia.title: Febrile neutropenia and infectious complications
febrileNeutropenia.lead: An algorithm for adults after the AGIHO/DGHO 2024 guideline: risk, the first line, what to do after 96 h, antifungal therapy and when to stop. Then the next step with negative cultures, acceptable combinations, infections by site and resistant pathogens (ECIL-4, AGIHO, ESCMID, IDSA 2026). Each step carries its grade.
febrileNeutropenia.agentsHint: Doses come from the labels (for febrile neutropenia or the stated use), for reserve agents from the IDSA 2026 table; where sources differ, both are shown. Without "calculate" it is reference only.
febrileNeutropenia.label: label
febrileNeutropenia.renal: Doses are for normal kidney function; the courses below show the label adjustment by creatinine clearance when renal impairment is ticked.
febrileNeutropenia.source: Source of the algorithm (full text and figures 1–4):
febrileNeutropenia.coursesHint: Doses from the labels. The antibiotics are calculated for 96 h, up to the mandatory review; the antifungals for the first days, then daily by the clinical response. The tree shows the label adjustment for the kidneys or liver when the patient condition is ticked.
